transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-01-10 | 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47 min
Attendees: Emily Nguyen (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Mapleworks Eng Manager), Rashida Khan (Mapleworks Head of Platform), Leo Ortega (Mapleworks SRE), Hannah Park (Mapleworks Security)
Links shared: https://redwood.app/runbooks/maple-onboard.pdf, https://redwood.app/benchmarks/vpc-checklist.xlsx (note: internal), security brief: https://redwood.app/security/soc2-summary.pdf

Auto summary (auto-generated): Kickoff to align on network/topology, compliance must-haves, pilot definition and timeline. Action items captured.

Topics:
- Networking: VPC peering, egress rules, NAT, private endpoints
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, audit logs retention
- Pilot: success criteria, traffic patterns, model selection (hosted vs dedicated)
- Integrations: terraform snippets, runbook, observability hooks

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Emily Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today, um this is Emily from Redwood, im joined by Marcus and Priya on our side. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jordan Kim: Good, thanks. Excited to get rolling. Sorry bit of background noise on my end.
[00:12] Marcus Li: No worries Jordan. We'll keep it tight, main goal today is to map out the first two weeks and the VPC plumbing.
[00:20] Rashida Khan: Great. We're eager to see how Redwood fits into our stack. A couple quick constraints up front — we need on-prem-like controls, data never leaves our VPC for the pilot and we'll need SSO + audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[00:36] Priya Rao: That makes sense. For the private path we have a Redwood Private option with a "customer-managed control plane", and we also support VPC peering for Redwood Dedicated — though I'll be explicit here, peering and private endpoints behave a bit different.
[00:51] Hannah Park: Quick clarifier, when you say "customer-managed control plane" is that fully air-gapped? Our legal team asked about air-gapped readiness.
[00:58] Priya Rao: Good question. We have an on-prem package that's designed for air-gapped environments, but we typically start with VPC peering + strict egress rules for pilots. Full air-gapped deployments take longer and need a different engagement.
[01:14] Leo Ortega: Ok noted. For the pilot we prefer peering first. What's the latency profile if we peer into Redwood Dedicated versus using hosted API?
[01:22] Emily Nguyen: In our experience, Dedicated with regional peering tends to give lower and more consistent p99 latency vs public hosted. But it depends on model size and batch settings. We'll share a short perf note — sorry the auto transcriber sometimes says "devoted" instead of Dedicated, ignore that.
[01:40] Jordan Kim: Haha ok thanks. Also we use GCP primarily, has anyone done a GCP -> Redwood Dedicated peering? Any gotchas?
[01:49] Priya Rao: Yes, we have several customers on GCP. Main gotchas are firewall rules for the private endpoint and ensuring NAT/route tables don't accidentally send traffic through a public gateway. We have terraform snippets in the runbook.
[02:05] Rashida Khan: Can you send that runbook now?
[02:07] Priya Rao: I'll share after, link in the notes — https://redwood.app/runbooks/maple-onboard.pdf.
[02:12] Marcus Li: Also we'll attach a lightweight template for the peering request and a sample terraform module.
[02:18] Hannah Park: On the security front — retention for audit logs, can we push logs to our Splunk? We need 365 day retention for some events.
[02:27] Priya Rao: Yes, we support pushing audit logs via our logging integration or you can pull them via our private streaming endpoint. Retention policy is configurable on the customer side if you run the Private offering; for hosted we retain standard audit logs but we can arrange longer retention with the enterprise add-on.
[02:44] Hannah Park: Good, can you confirm where keys are stored? KMS? HSM?
[02:48] Emily Nguyen: Keys can be customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, and we support HSM integrations for certain enterprise customers. We'll include the security brief with specifics (SOC2 scope, encryption in transit + at rest).
[02:58] Jordan Kim: Quick note — our infra lead is on PTO next week, so timeline might slip if we require heavy network configs. Can we define a minimal pilot that requires minimal infra changes?
[03:08] Marcus Li: Absolutely — typical minimal pilot is: 1) sandbox VPC peering to Redwood Dedicated, 2) a single small model endpoint, 3) a limited traffic window with a handful of test prompts. That usually surfaces integration issues without heavy lift.
[03:24] Leo Ortega: What's the token cost profile for a small model vs a larger one? We're trying to compare cost-per-call for inference.
[03:31] Priya Rao: We'll send a cost guidance chart. Roughly speaking, smaller models cut compute cost but might increase latency for complex prompts; quantized variants can reduce token cost. Redwood Optimize can also recommend batching windows and quantization profiles tailored to your workload.
[03:50] Jordan Kim: Can you explain the batching aspect? Our product needs low tail latency.
[03:54] Priya Rao: Sure — our runtime does continuous batching and prefix caching. For low tail latency you can constrain max batch size and enable KV cache. There's a trade-off: smaller batches = better latency, larger batches = lower cost. We'll recommend settings per your QPS distribution.
[04:11] Rashida Khan: Who's owner for observability hookup — cloudwatch or prometheus exporter?
[04:16] Marcus Li: We support both. For most infra teams we provide a Prometheus metrics endpoint for Dedicated and Private; hosted can stream metrics to CloudWatch or third-party exporters.
[04:27] Hannah Park: Can we require SAML SSO for admin console access during the pilot?
[04:31] Emily Nguyen: Yes, SAML SSO for admin can be enforced. We'll capture the SAML metadata format in the runbook.
[04:37] Jordan Kim: Great. Next, pilot success criteria — can we list those out?
[04:40] Marcus Li: I'll propose a first draft: 1) <100ms median latency for small prompts, 2) end-to-end integration with our auth and audit pipeline, 3) successful VPC peering with test calls from your VPC, 4) cost per 1k requests aligns with target budget. We can refine.
[04:58] Jordan Kim: Sounds good. For the model itself, we plan to start with a reranking/embedding use-case. Is Redwood good for embeddings at scale?
[05:07] Priya Rao: Yes — we have an embeddings pipeline and dedicated endpoints that are optimized for vector workloads and can scale horizontally. Also caching for embeddings is less common but we do support batching.
[05:20] Hannah Park: Any compliance docs upfront for Legal?
[05:24] Emily Nguyen: Yes, we'll share the SOC2 summary, encryption whitepaper, and our standard DPA. I'll put those links in the follow-up.
[05:31] Rashida Khan: Regarding network egress, we need to make sure no PII leaves our VPC; is that something Redwood can commit to?
[05:39] Priya Rao: For Dedicated/Private where compute runs in your network boundary or peered VPC, you control data residency. For hosted API, data leaves our environment. We'll mark that clearly in the runbook and in the SOW if we go that route.
[05:54] Jordan Kim: Ok that answers a lot. Timeline question: if we start the pilot next week what's realistic?
[05:59] Marcus Li: If infra is available, a minimal pilot can be live in 7-14 business days. Given your infra owner PTO, I'd expect 2-3 weeks.
[06:09] Jordan Kim: Fine.
[06:11] -- CROSSTALK --
[06:13] Leo Ortega: One more network question — do you require mutual TLS between our services and the Redwood endpoint?
[06:18] Priya Rao: We support mTLS as an option. For peered Dedicated endpoints we commonly use mTLS plus private IP allow lists.
[06:26] Hannah Park: Good. Also please confirm RBAC granularity — can we restrict model deploy permissions to a small team?
[06:32] Emily Nguyen: Yes, RBAC is token-level. You can create roles, limit deploy/rollout capabilities, and audit actions.
[06:40] Jordan Kim: Anything else on network?
[06:42] Rashida Khan: Not from me.
[06:43] Marcus Li: Alright quick recap of owners: Priya will send the runbook + terraform snippets; Marcus will set up the pilot success doc and calendar invites; Jordan/Leo will provision test VPC and share details; Hannah will pull security requirements and confirm KMS approach.
[06:58] Jordan Kim: I'll try to have the VPC info by Friday but if not it'll be early next week.
[07:03] Marcus Li: Thanks.
[07:06] -- [07:06 - 15:00] Further detailed questions on specific firewall rules, sample terraform, and metrics schema. (transcription compressed) --
[15:00] Priya Rao: Noting a couple implementation gotchas: 1) route table prioritization on GCP can cause egress if NAT isn't correctly configured, 2) some customers forget to open the internal firewall for the private endpoint port — we'll include a checklist.
[15:21] Leo Ortega: Appreciate that. Also would you run a very small bench test from our infra team? We can schedule a 1-hour test where Redwood runs a quick endpoint and we run a battery of concurrency tests.
[15:32] Priya Rao: Yes that's standard. We'll do a handshake test then a perf test. We'll also share a lightweight results template so it's easy to compare.
[15:40] Rashida Khan: For the results template can you include per-call latency percentiles and tokenization breakdown?
[15:45] Priya Rao: Yep. We'll include p50/p95/p99 and token breakdown, and an ops checklist for reproducing.
[15:52] Jordan Kim: One odd question: our procurement team asked about vendor lock-in — how easy is it to migrate away later?
[15:58] Emily Nguyen: We document end-of-engagement export paths for model configs and usage logs. Because you control model version pins and have access to logs, migration is mostly a matter of provisioning replacements. We try to avoid proprietary hooks where possible.
[16:11] Hannah Park: Anything around data deletion guarantees after pilot termination?
[16:15] Emily Nguyen: Yes, for Dedicated/Private you control data retention. For hosted we provide documented deletion procedures and can coordinate wipe and attestation post-contract. We'll add that to the security brief.
[16:28] Marcus Li: Ok I think we're converging. Any blockers from the customer side?
[16:33] Jordan Kim: mainly infra availability and confirming legal requirements.
[16:36] Rashida Khan: Also we need to confirm that the pilot will not trigger extra exposure to our production creds — we will use a service account with limited privileges.
[16:44] Priya Rao: That's exactly what we recommend — a scoped service account for the pilot.
[16:47] Marcus Li: Last piece — cadence. We'll do weekly 30-minute syncs, first one next Wednesday, I'll send invites.
[16:55] Jordan Kim: works for me.
[16:57] Emily Nguyen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with runbook, security brief, terraform snippets and the pilot success doc.
[17:05] Rashida Khan: Appreciate it.
[17:07] -- Meeting ended --

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions and compressed sections; some technical passages condensed.
